agree.reason: The concession on the science and the 2016 figures make the comment credible, but commissioners who trust staff get no stock-based reason to take three fish over two and none of the captain's concrete offers (trip logs, a reporting-app trial), so most would stay with staff.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the unsupported claim that every boat will close, and its figures are accurate, but 'never fully recovered' stretches the brief's single two-year data point, 'a private angler still goes fishing' is asserted without support, and the separate for-hire limit is an ask the captain never named.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives the 19% drop and the roughly $29,000 loss correctly, but leaves the 41 of 70 as raw counts rather than 'nearly 6 in 10', and never states the boat's roughly $144,000 season revenue or the harbor-wide stake.

right_comparison.reason: It sets the charter fleet's 9% against private boats' 80%, but never says how little cutting the charter limit adds to rebuilding the stock, or what a three-fish limit or shorter season would do to the 78% figure.

qualification.reason: The one-year review has no metric, threshold or consequence tied to it, and the comment does not offer the trip logs or app trial that would give the commission something to check.

objections.reason: It heads off the 'you're attacking our science' objection, but not the obvious ones that a charter group's own customer survey is self-serving and that his bookings came back after 2016, both of which the logs offer and the 70%-booked fact could have helped answer.

fit.reason: At about 340 words it fits a two-minute public comment and is built for speaking, though it leaves [NAME] and [HARBOR] placeholders where the captain's name and boat were available.
